records.deidentified_narrative: see related sn# [phone]. this is dallas police dept. traffic fatality # 109 for the year 2021. unit 1 was traveling in a s/w direction on 8100 lyndon b. johnson exit ramp. that leads to s/b n. central expressway ( [roadway] 75 ). unit 2 was parked and unoccupied along the southeast shoulder near the retaining wall with its overhead amber wrecker lights flashing. unit 3 was being towed by unit 2. unit 4 ( pedestrian ) was standing to the right of unit 3. driver of unit 1 failed to slow or move for vehicle displaying emergency lights by veering to the left onto [roadway] and colliding the front left and left front qtr of unit 1 into the back right and right back qtr of unit 3. the impact into unit 3, sent unit 3 to the left causing the left front qtr to strike the s/e retaining wall. after colliding into unit 3, the front left of unit 1 collided into the back right of unit 2 and struck unit 4 ( pedestrian ) causing unit 4 to be thrown into the air and over the s/e retaining wall and onto the e/b traffic lanes of the texpress that was 60 ft below. unit 1 travelled about 60 ft. s/w of the accident and struck the left front qtr of unit 1 into the s/e retaining wall. the impact of unit 1 into unit 4 and the fall caused unit 4 to succumb to his injuries. when rescue 57 arrived on scene, rescue personnel did not find any vital signs on unit 4 at 10:01 p. m. . after the collision, driver of unit 1 got out of unit 1 and walked down the exit ramp until she found a dallas police officer. driver of unit 1 was found to be under the influence of alcohol. the on call vehicle crimes unit detective was notified and came out and took photos of the scene. the traffic watch commander was notified and came out. the scene was laser scanned. the crash scene and all interviews were recorded on body worn camera. the video and/or photos were saved to evidence. com on id# 21-1645588. i/o took digital photos and placed them into dataworks. this report will be incomplete pending the blood toxicology results for driver of unit 1. ** on [date], this supplement was made to add the blood toxicology results for driver of unit 1. driver 1's blood results had the presence of ethanol ( 0. 060 g/100ml ). i/o also added the factor of 68 for unit 1. driver 1's blood showed the presence of drugs ( 2. 2 ng/ml tetrahydrocannabinol, 38. 9 ng/ml carboxytetrahydrocannabinol and levetiracetam was detected). unit 4 ( pedestrian) had the slight presence of ethanol ( ethanol: 0. 017 g/100 ) and a trace of marihuana/cannabinoids sample unsuitable. ** this report is now complete. ** on [date], this supplement was made to add the blood test results for unit 4. ** on [date], i/o printed off crash drawing. **

records.deidentified_narrative: driver unit 1 advised she was turning left in the parking lot, did not see the pedestrian (unit 2) and struck her with the front left portion of her vehicle, causing unit 2's left foot to be run over by the front driver's side wheel. unit 2 advised she was walking in the parking lot to enter the costco store when she was struck from lightly behind and on her right side, causing her to fall to the ground. upon falling to the ground, unit 2 advised driver unit 1 ran over her left foot. the driver of unit 1 immediately stopped to check on unit 2 but reportedly stopped while still on unit 2's foot and had to get back into her vehicle and move off of unit 2's foot. unit 2 was awake and conscious upon pd arrival. upon initial patient assessment i did not observe any bleeding or obvious visible injury. patient was able to move her toes and had feeling in her left foot. plano fd arrived moments later and took over medical treatment/assessment of unit 2. unit 2 was transported by plano fd med 1 to medical city plano for medical evaluation/treatment. plano csi responded to mcp to photographically document injuries to unit 2's foot. this included some visible abrasions to the top of her left foot and her left knee. unit 2 complained of pain in her left hip as well. based on unit 1 and unit 2's statements, it is possible that unit 1's view of unit 2 was partially obstructed by the ""a-pillar"" and driver's side mirror of unit 1 and as unit 1 stated, simply did not see unit 2 as she was making the left turn.
